questions.q: Why not repeat “use Rust” in every turn?
questions.a: It's still a request the model weighs against its habit, paid for on every turn. A check works whether the model remembers or not.
Only Python that would ship. A throwaway script to compare two outputs is the agent thinking with a tool. Block Python files landing in the project, and let cargo test decide when the task is done.

questions.q: Isn't the real fix retraining the model?
questions.a: Longer term, maybe: Twist et al. call for targeted fine-tuning and more varied training data. But you don't control that. You do control the repo, the hooks and the tests, today.

questions.q: Why doesn't one perfect port prove the agent will keep using Rust?
questions.a: During the port it had the Python original to copy and a fresh request. Later tasks have neither, and the model's Python prior is still there.

questions.q: Name two likely sources of the Python prior.
questions.a: The code models learn from, and the practice tasks coding agents train and are tested on. A model's training data isn't public, but the public training sets and benchmarks we can see are mostly Python.

questions.q: Put these in order from weakest to strongest: a hook that blocks Python, a chat message, the project instructions file.
questions.a: Chat message, then instructions file, then hook. The first two are context the model weighs and can forget. The hook acts whatever the model decides.
